items.title: Ken Peplowski interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Well I wanted to ask you about “Steppin’ with Peps.” Most people call you “Peps?” [INTERVIEWEE] A lot of people do. Pep, Peps, yeah.

ctx.x: Oh yeah. And sometimes it’s the wrong thing to do. But you do it because you’re panicking and you’re trying to overcompensate. Sometimes it’s best to try and let yourself relax and just say, as I pointed out before, I’m going to ignore these people and just play for myself. Like if I was playing in a room or if I was rehearsing for Benny Goodman, I’m my own rhythm section, played the changes my own way, and then it really works well. And then you can kind of lift them up sometimes. Occasionally. Not always.
Well I wanted to ask you about “Steppin’ with Peps.” Most people call you “Peps?”
A lot of people do. Pep, Peps, yeah.
